decision: Make deployment-manifest verification executable QA authority at the Phase-1 boundary
winner: manifest-bound fail-before-qrexec regressions plus workflow coverage

comparisons.correctness: insufficient because deployment manifest drift is not exercised
comparisons.robustness: can leave configuration provenance regressions undetected
comparisons.qa: failed to cover a required production argument

comparisons.approach: manifest-bound fail-before-qrexec regressions plus workflow coverage
comparisons.correctness: covers service, coordinator, user, uid, git sha, readOnly and state-changing-operation policy
comparisons.robustness: fails closed before qrexec on manifest absence or drift
comparisons.latency: local test-only comparisons; no production round trip
comparisons.qa: strongest; closes both test-fixture and workflow-trigger gaps

comparisons.approach: defer manifest validation until real-Qubes integration
comparisons.correctness: late discovery of deterministic contract failures
comparisons.robustness: mixes deployment provenance defects with transport/policy failures
comparisons.resourceUse: requires Qubes execution for basic contract defects

lessons: Adding a fail-closed production argument without updating the happy-path fixture creates a deterministic hidden test failure when CI is unavailable.
A workflow path filter that omits a security-authority file can silently skip the only QA intended to validate it.
Configuration provenance should be rejected before qrexec so invalid deployments produce zero remote invocations.
safety: Read-only synthetic Qubes qualification only; no financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflows, or weakened controls.
